items.title: Critical, detection, and quantification levels
items.statement: For a response law P_c indexed by nonnegative concentration c, define an exact critical level L_C by P_0(X>L_C)=alpha, a detection limit L_D as the least positive c with P_c(X<=L_C)=beta when it exists, and a quantification limit L_Q as the least positive c satisfying the declared coefficient-of-variation criterion CV(c)<=k_Q when it exists.

references.title: A Century of Excellence in Measurements, Standards, and Technology: A Chronicle of Selected NBS/NIST Publications 1901–2000, NIST SP 958, pp. 177–179 (printed pp. 164–166)
H. Cantwell (ed.), Eurachem Guide: The Fitness for Purpose of Analytical Methods, 3rd ed. (2025), §5.3.1

items.title: The standard normal CDF has unique symmetric quantiles
items.statement: For Z with the standard normal law and Phi(x)=P(Z<=x), Phi is continuous and strictly increasing from 0 to 1 and P(Z=x)=0 for every x. Thus for every q in (0,1) there is a unique z_q with Phi(z_q)=q, and z_(1-q)=-z_q.

references.title: A Century of Excellence in Measurements, Standards, and Technology: A Chronicle of Selected NBS/NIST Publications 1901–2000, NIST SP 958, pp. 177–179 (printed pp. 164–166)
H. Cantwell (ed.), Eurachem Guide: The Fitness for Purpose of Analytical Methods, 3rd ed. (2025), Annex B

items.title: Location-scale normal laws have their stated mean and variance
items.statement: Assume AC. If X has law N(m,sigma^2), then E[X]=m and Var(X)=sigma^2.

references.title: A Century of Excellence in Measurements, Standards, and Technology: A Chronicle of Selected NBS/NIST Publications 1901–2000, NIST SP 958, pp. 177–179 (printed pp. 164–166)
H. Cantwell (ed.), Eurachem Guide: The Fitness for Purpose of Analytical Methods, 3rd ed. (2025), §5.3.4

items.title: Exact limits in the known-blank equal-variance normal model
items.statement: Assume AC, sigma_0>0, 0<alpha,beta<1/2, k_Q>0, and X_c~N(c,sigma_0^2) for every concentration c>=0. With the positive decision rule X>L_C and coefficient-of-variation criterion CV(c)<=k_Q, the exact limits are L_C=z_(1-alpha)sigma_0, L_D=(z_(1-alpha)+z_(1-beta))sigma_0, and L_Q=sigma_0/k_Q.

references.title: A Century of Excellence in Measurements, Standards, and Technology: A Chronicle of Selected NBS/NIST Publications 1901–2000, NIST SP 958, pp. 177–179 (printed pp. 164–166)
H. Cantwell (ed.), Eurachem Guide: The Fitness for Purpose of Analytical Methods, 3rd ed. (2025), §5.3.1 and Annex B

items.title: Known-blank normal limits at five-percent error and ten-percent CV
items.statement: In the known-blank equal-variance normal model, alpha=beta=0.05 and CV tolerance k_Q=0.10 give L_C=z_0.95 sigma_0, L_D=2z_0.95 sigma_0, and L_Q=10 sigma_0. NIST SP958 Table I reports the corresponding rounded well-known-blank row 1.64 sigma_0, 3.29 sigma_0, and 10 sigma_0.

references.title: A Century of Excellence in Measurements, Standards, and Technology: A Chronicle of Selected NBS/NIST Publications 1901–2000, NIST SP 958, pp. 177–179 (printed pp. 164–166)
H. Cantwell (ed.), Eurachem Guide: The Fitness for Purpose of Analytical Methods, 3rd ed. (2025), Annex B

items.title: An estimated blank increases the effective normal scale
items.statement: If the corrected response is explicitly modeled as D_c~N(c,sigma_0^2+tau^2), with tau^2>0 the declared additional blank-estimation variance contribution, then the exact normal formulas use sigma_eff=sqrt(sigma_0^2+tau^2) in place of sigma_0, so all three limits increase.

references.title: H. Cantwell (ed.), Eurachem Guide: The Fitness for Purpose of Analytical Methods, 3rd ed. (2025), §5.3.2 and §5.3.5

items.title: Detection-limit assumptions and left-censored readings
items.statement: For Y_c~N(c,sigma_0^2(1+rho c)^2), rho>=0, the blank critical level is z_(1-alpha)sigma_0. A target beta false-negative limit exists finitely exactly when z_(1-beta)rho sigma_0<1, and then L_D=(L_C+z_(1-beta)sigma_0)/(1-z_(1-beta)rho sigma_0). The CV criterion has a finite L_Q exactly when k_Q>rho sigma_0, in which case L_Q=sigma_0/(k_Q-rho sigma_0). A report that only records Y<=L_C contributes the probability Phi((L_C-c)/(sigma_0(1+rho c))) to the likelihood.

references.title: H. Cantwell (ed.), Eurachem Guide: The Fitness for Purpose of Analytical Methods, 3rd ed. (2025), §§5.3.1–5.3.5 and Annex B
